preamble: In the western and south-central dialects of Asturian and Leonese, the palatal lateral /ʎ/ (standard Asturian ll, from Latin initial L- and medial -LL-) is realized as an obstruent, the 'che vaqueira', written ḷḷ. Its commonest realization is the voiceless retroflex affricate [ʈʂ], found in Aller, Quirós and elsewhere; other areas have [ɖʐ], [ɖ] or [ts].

examples.note: Standard Asturian has [ʎ]; che vaqueira dialects realize the same phoneme as a retroflex affricate. Medial -LL- gives the same sound (mueḷḷe 'soft' < Latin molle).
The che vaqueira also occurs where /ʎ/ comes from Latin CL- and PL- (ḷḷantar 'to plant').

sources: Wikipedia (2026). Che vaqueira (Spanish Wikipedia, citing García Arias, X. Ll. (2003). Gramática histórica de la lengua asturiana). https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Che_vaqueira
